title: Keystore tinkering and SOC2 readiness musing
content:
Purpose: quick brain dump while mapping keystore/kms hygiene to SOC2 evidence for private deployments and Dedicated clusters. Working notes, not polished.

Top-level goal:
- produce a minimal artefact set that auditors accept for KMS + key lifecycle controls across Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.

High-level concerns (questions to answer):
- Who is the canonical owner for customer key material in Private deployments? (ops? customer? product?)
- What evidence shows key rotation happened on schedule for Dedicated pools? (rotation logs + PRs + retention)
- How do we show separation of duties for keystore access (devs vs ops vs SRE)? Need policy + audit logs + approve flow.
- For HSM-backed keys: what vendor certs/attestations do we accept? do we store vendor firmware attestation artifacts?

Quick mapping notes (rough, for discussion):
- CC: Logical and Physical Access Controls -> KMS admin role definitions + IAM policies (show role docs + policy JSON + last_modified).
- CC: Change Management -> PRs that update KMS config / configures rotation schedules + deploy runbook. Attach PR links + release notes.
- CC: System Operations -> rotation job logs (cron history) + alerts for rotation failures (pagerduty incidents).
- CC: Incident Response -> example incident with key compromise simulation (postmortem) + notifications.

Evidence candidates (what to collect):
- policy/key-management.md (human-readable policy) -> need canonical copy in Confluence + snapshot in evidence zip.
- IAM snapshots for key roles (last 6 months).
- KMS rotation job logs (start time, end time, rotated key IDs, actor).
- HSM vendor attestation and certificate file (if used).
- Automation pipeline runbooks (terraform state showing key resources).
- Sample anonymized audit logs showing key access from one of the Dedicated clusters.
- PR + review trail for rotation interval change (shows approval).

Implementation thoughts / rough TODOs:
- [ ] Add a scripted exporter that pulls: IAM bindings for KMS roles, rotation job logs, and recent access logs into a single evidence bundle. (owner: @juno)
- [ ] Create a templated readme for auditors that maps each piece of evidence to SOC2 criteria (owner: @samir).
- [ ] Identify 2 Dedicated customers to use as test cases (screenshot + policy doc) so auditors can see real-world config differences (owner: eng-sols).
- [ ] Draft a minimal policy snippet for "Key rotation frequency" and decide cutoff for rotation exceptions.

Edge cases / gotchas:
- We rotate key material for model caches and for customer data—do we treat those differently in evidence? probably yes: separate categories.
- Offline rotation (air-gapped/private on-prem) needs manual log ingestion process documented; auditors will expect chain-of-custody notes.
- Multi-tenant nodes: ensure logs show tenant-scoped key access; otherwise we risk failing SOD (segregation).

Brainstormed control text (very rough):
- "All cryptographic keys used to protect customer-sensitive data must be managed by the Redwood KMS framework or a customer-approved HSM. Keys must be rotated at interval N unless documented exception approved by Security and Product. Administrative access to KMS must be limited via IAM roles and reviewed quarterly."

Sample audit play-by-play we should be able to show (happy path):
1) Confluence page: Key Management Policy (timestamped snapshot)
2) IAM export: role bindings for kms-admin / kms-operator / kms-reader (CSV)
3) Rotation job run: logs showing old_key_id -> new_key_id, job actor (automation-service-account), PR link that triggered config update if any
4) Access log: one sample call to Encrypt/Decrypt with service account + tenant id (redacted)
5) Post-rotation smoke test: results (success/fail) and any incidents raised.

Notes to self re: tooling:
- Could leverage existing evidence exporter (EVID-collector v0.3) but it currently omits IAM snapshots. Add IAM plugin.
- Need to keep sample logs short and redacted. Create a redact script that replaces tenant IDs with stable tokens.

Open questions for sync with Security PM (Juno):
- What rotation interval are we committing to for Dedicated vs Hosted? (default 1y?)
- Will auditors accept automation-service-account proofs or do they require human approval evidence for each rotation?
- For Private (customer-managed KMS), what is minimum evidence we can request without violating customer autonomy?

Meeting prep for Thursday (sync with @juno, @samir, @marina):
- Walk through the proposed evidence bundle layout (I will bring sample export).
- Decide on rotation intervals & exceptions policy.
- Assign owners for export scripts and Confluence mapping page.

Random scratch ideas:
- Could we provide a "KMS evidence kit" in the Console (button: Download compliance bundle) for Dedicated customers? Might be a product feature but could save time.
- Consider a short questionnaire for Private customers to self-attest key management practices; store responses as signed PDF.

References / links to pull into formal doc later:
- CONFLUENCE: Key Management Guidelines (linked above)
- JIRA: SEC-4123 (keystore rotation improvements)
- PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/789 (rotation automation work)

Last quick sketches (non-linear):
- retention window for logs = 2 years? auditors sometimes want 12 months minimum but infra team wary of cost. Need compromise.
- backup of key metadata (not key material): should be versioned and immutable snapshot per quarter.

-- end of brain dump --

Notes: transform this into three deliverables: (1) auditor-readme + mapping table, (2) export script (proof-of-concept), (3) policy doc with rotation schedule and emergency key revocation flow.

Ping me if you want to co-edit before Thurs.

Ian
